investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T08:09–08:16Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the createAgent call.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. Only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster are eligible for peer-pod scheduling (the other 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and both of those nodes report zero remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, the eval runner never receives a running VM, and all required evidence fields remain empty.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, so the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before capacity is even checked.

Tertiary — a surge or leak of existing remote-agent or peer-pod workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them (e.g., stuck cleanup, failed teardown of prior eval runs), leaving no capacity for new pods.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the two kata-capable nodes may have been sized with insufficient vm-slot limits for the current eval concurrency, meaning the cluster was never large enough to absorb simultaneous probe runs.

Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 carry this resource and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"; the other 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector and preemption is not possible. As a result, every eval attempt to provision a remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable for 120–145 seconds before timing out, preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling evidence unreachable. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T08:09–08:16Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the eval runner could not advance past the createAgent call.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. Only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster are eligible for peer-pod scheduling (the other 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and both of those nodes report zero remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, the eval runner never receives a running VM, and all required evidence fields remain empty.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-03 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: 0/6 nodes are available due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from ever instantiating a remote agent, which in turn means no evidence is produced and the expected-output contract cannot be satisfied.
